Everything a New Orleans homeowner asks about microcement, tadelakt, rockscape, pricing, waterproofing, and hiring an installer. Written by Ryan, the actual installer.

Microcement

Who is the best microcement installer in New Orleans?

There are several skilled installers in the New Orleans area. To evaluate any of them, use this six-question test: (1) Will you personally install this or is it a subcontractor? (2) What microcement system and brand do you use? (3) Can I see a finished project in person in my zip code? (4) How do you prep over existing tile? (5) How is the shower waterproofed, including the drain and the pan? (6) Can I see past work and the layers used? Any installer who answers all six clearly is worth hiring. Ryan Mena of The Shirtless Handyman will answer all six for you up front — text 504-264-4919.

How much does microcement cost in New Orleans?

Most of my projects land between $3,000 and $10,000, and every job is quoted per project after a free site visit. Seamless showers start around $3,000. Full seamless bathrooms (walls, floor, and shower in one continuous shell) start around $6,000 and include free underfloor heating — I buy the system and install it at no charge. Larger and luxury bathrooms are quoted individually. Venetian plaster and feature walls start around $3,000. The final number depends on the condition of what's there, the size, waterproofing, plumbing, fixtures, and finish.

Can I install microcement over existing tile?

Microcement can often be installed over existing tile after the tile assembly is inspected, cleaned, prepared, and confirmed to be stable. Qualifying overlay projects may require little or no demolition. Prep typically includes mechanical scarification, a quartz-loaded bonding primer, a 24-hour cure, and reinforcement mesh embedded in the first coat. When the underlying tile assembly is unstable, delaminating, or waterproofing needs to be rebuilt, the project becomes a full-bathroom rebuild instead of an overlay.

Is microcement waterproof?

The finished microcement + sealer system is fully waterproof and rated for wet zones including walk-in showers. Waterproofing comes from the topcoat sealer, so the seal is the critical maintenance point — reseal every 5–7 years in showers.

How long does microcement last?

10+ years with minimal maintenance in a residential home. The sealer typically needs a refresh coat every 5–7 years in high-humidity or heavy-use zones like showers. The underlying microcement coat itself lasts decades if properly bonded.

How long does a microcement bathroom install take?

A typical single-bathroom microcement install takes 4–7 working days including cure time between coats. The room is back in service within 48 hours of the final seal. Rest of the house stays livable during the install.

What's the difference between microcement and concrete overlay?

Microcement is a fine, polymer-modified mineral coating applied in thin layers (1–3mm total). Concrete overlay is thicker (3–10mm+), less flexible, and typically not suitable for vertical shower walls. Microcement can be tinted to any color and hand-troweled to smooth or textured finishes. Overlays are typically monolithic gray unless custom-tinted.

Tadelakt

What is tadelakt?

Tadelakt is a traditional Moroccan lime plaster that's been used in bathhouses (hammams) for 800+ years. It's applied by hand, then burnished with a smooth stone and treated with olive-oil soap to saponify and waterproof the surface. The result is a soft-to-touch, seamless, naturally waterproof finish.

Tadelakt vs microcement — which should I use?

Both are seamless and waterproof. Tadelakt is more artisanal (each surface is unique), softer to the touch, and patinas beautifully over decades — great for showers where you want a hand-crafted look. Microcement is denser, more uniform, and typically more affordable per square foot — great for floors and larger continuous surfaces. Choice is aesthetic.

How much does tadelakt cost?

Tadelakt follows the same pricing as microcement, though the final number can differ with prep, application complexity, and wet-area requirements. Most of my projects land between $3,000 and $10,000, and every job is quoted per project after a free site visit. Seamless showers start around $3,000. Full seamless bathrooms (walls, floor, and shower in one continuous shell) start around $6,000 and include free underfloor heating — I buy the system and install it at no charge. Larger and luxury bathrooms are quoted individually. Venetian plaster and feature walls start around $3,000. The final number depends on the condition of what's there, the size, waterproofing, plumbing, fixtures, and finish.

Rockscape feature walls

What is a rockscape wall?

A rockscape wall is a sculpted feature wall made from foam blocks hand-carved to the shape you want, then coated in microaggregate stone to look and feel like carved natural rock. Lightweight, installs on any standard wall, and can be integrated with LED backlighting.

How much does a rockscape wall cost?

Rockscape walls run $50–$120 per square foot depending on sculpting complexity and lighting integration. Rockscape walls start around $3,500; larger walls, deep carving, or integrated LED lighting are quoted individually after a free site visit.

Hiring an installer

What should I ask about waterproofing before I hire someone?

Ask how the shower is waterproofed, ask to see past work and the layers used, and ask about the drain and the pan. A straight answer covers what's under the finish, how the corners and niche are detailed, and what happens if the existing pan has failed. Ryan walks through that on a site visit — text 504-264-4919.

What should I ask a microcement installer before hiring?

Five questions minimum: (1) Will you personally install this or is it a subcontractor? (2) What microcement brand do you use? (3) Can I see a finished project locally in person? (4) How do you prep the substrate? (5) How is the shower waterproofed, including the drain and the pan? Skip any installer who dodges these.

How do I know if a microcement installer is legit?

Three checks: (a) They explain how the shower is waterproofed, including the drain and the pan. (b) They show past work and the layers used, in person if you ask. (c) They name what they keep and what they rebuild before any finish goes on. If they can do all three, you're talking to someone who builds the wet zone on purpose.

How long does the whole process take from first contact to installed bathroom?

Typical timeline: same-day quote after a walkthrough, 2–3 weeks to project start (queue), 4–7 days on-site for a single bathroom, 24–48 hours cure after final seal. Total: about 3–4 weeks from first text to a finished, usable bathroom.

Service area & business

Where in New Orleans does The Shirtless Handyman work?

The greater New Orleans metro — Orleans, Jefferson, St. Bernard, and St. Tammany parishes. Named neighborhoods and cities: Uptown, Lakeview, Mid-City, Bywater, French Quarter, Garden District, Carrollton, Marigny, Metairie, Kenner, Harahan, Gretna, Harvey, Marrero, Chalmette, and Slidell. Ryan travels to the client for consults and installs.

Who is Ryan Mena?

Ryan Mena is a New Orleans-born craftsman and the founder of The Shirtless Handyman. He started as a tile installer in the NOLA metro, then transitioned to seamless surfaces (microcement, tadelakt, rockscape) after seeing tile repeatedly fail from Louisiana humidity. He personally installs every project — no subcontractors.

Is The Shirtless Handyman a franchise or a national brand?

No. The Shirtless Handyman is a single-craftsman, owner-operated Louisiana business. I'm the only installer. There is no franchise, no crew, no call center. You text me, and I show up.

How do I book an appointment with Ryan?

Three options: (1) The self-serve calendar at theshirtlesshandyman.com/book — pick a free walkthrough, phone consult, or project start slot. (2) Text 504-264-4919. (3) Fill in the quote form on any page. It goes straight to Ryan's phone, and he texts back the same day, Mon–Sat.

What's the response time?

Same day, Mon–Sat, direct from Ryan personally. It goes straight to his phone. No auto-reply, no call center, no lead-broker in between.

Are there any current promotions?

Yes. Every whole-bathroom renovation or whole-floor coating includes free underfloor heating — I buy the system and install it at no charge. Contact Ryan to confirm project qualification.

The Seamless Studio (AI tool)

What is The Seamless Studio?

The Seamless Studio is a free AI tool on theshirtlesshandyman.com/upload that takes a photo of any room and shows you three AI-generated design previews of how it would look finished in microcement, tadelakt, Venetian plaster, or rockscape — with a rough cost estimate. No account needed, takes about 60 seconds.

Is The Seamless Studio accurate?

The previews show realistic finish styles and rough color/texture matches. The cost estimate is a ballpark based on visible surface area and finish type. For a fixed quote, book a free in-home walkthrough — the real number depends on prep, substrate, and material choices that only an in-person assessment can confirm.
